ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The udumbara flower is invoked as something that appears only rarely.
EvidenceBody: Dahui says it appears once in its season. Other records apply the flower to a person, a present occasion, or a folded appearance; the word can praise rarity without every use naming the same meeting or figure.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: Chan speakers use the rare-bloom comparison for difficult-to-encounter appearances and occasions.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: Dahui’s T47 line anchors rarity; the entry does not attribute the other personal and poetic uses to him.
